- Ensure your messaging app has storage and SMS permissions
- Reboot your device if we make any settings changes

Share your verification details and answers to the questions above, and we’ll get started.

Got it. Being on a 2G network is likely why MMS isn’t working—it needs at least 3G. Since you’re abroad with a weak signal, let’s get your device onto a faster network and then adjust a few settings.

Step 1: Switch to 4G/5G network mode
- On your phone: go to Settings > Mobile Network/Cellular > Network Mode/Preferred network type
- Choose “5G/4G/LTE” (or “4G/5G preferred”). Avoid “2G/3G only” or “2G only.”
- After changing, wait 20–30 seconds to let it reconnect.

Step 2: Recheck status
- Please run again:
  - check_status_bar
  - check_network_status
  - can_send_mms

Tell me what network type it shows now and whether signal strength improved. If it’s still 2G or very weak, we can try toggling Airplane Mode once more to force a fresh network registration:
- Run toggle_airplane_mode to turn it on, wait 10 seconds, then run toggle_airplane_mode again to turn it off.

If you get a 3G/4G/5G connection and still can’t send MMS, we’ll proceed to:
- Check APN settings and reset if needed
- Turn off Wi‑Fi Calling temporarily
- Ensure messaging app permissions

Let me know the results after Step 2.

events.action:
Great work getting to a solid 5G connection. Next, let’s check the APN settings, messaging app permissions, and Wi‑Fi Calling—those are the most common causes when you have signal but MMS still won’t work.

Please run these in order and share each result:

1) Check APN settings
- Run: check_apn_settings
- Tell me if the APN name looks correct and, importantly, whether the MMSC URL is set.

2) Check messaging app permissions
- Run: check_app_permissions with app_name set to “messaging”
- Let me know if “storage” and “sms” are granted.

3) Check Wi‑Fi Calling status
- Run: check_wifi_calling_status
- Let me know if Wi‑Fi Calling is ON or OFF.

Based on what you find, we’ll do this:
- If the APN/ MMSC looks wrong or missing: I’ll guide you to reset APN settings, then we’ll reboot.
- If storage or SMS permissions are missing: I’ll guide you to grant them.
- If Wi‑Fi Calling is ON: We’ll turn it OFF temporarily because it can interfere with MMS on some networks.

Also, for the test: please ensure Wi‑Fi is off and you’re on mobile data when you try to send a picture message. Let me know the results from those three checks, and we’ll continue.

- Then try sending a picture message on mobile data.
